name: Liquid-nitrogen spray tunnel freezing of whole litchi at -40 to -70 °C (full-cone vs hollow-cone nozzles, 800/1200 rpm fans) to a -18 °C core
plain_name: Quick-freeze whole litchi fruit in a liquid-nitrogen spray tunnel without cracking the peel
description: Taguchi optimisation on a liquid-nitrogen quick-freezing tunnel (Shenzhen De jie li Cryogenic Technology): pre-treated whole litchis (35.2 mm average diameter, 36.09 mm height, 23.9 g) were frozen at tunnel temperatures of -40, -50, -60 and -70 °C with two nozzle types and two fan speeds until the core reached -18 °C; crack ratio, freezing time and nitrogen consumption fell as the tunnel temperature was lowered.
keywords: Quick-freeze whole litchi fruit in a liquid-nitrogen spray tunnel without cracking the peel

sources.citation: Abdeen MA, Zheng Z, Cheng X, et al., Wu W (2025). Enhancing rapid nitrogen freezer performance for Litchi fruit: a Taguchi-based approach to reduce cracking, time, and nitrogen consumption. Scientific Reports 15:11186. doi:10.1038/s41598-025-95215-3

reported_equipment: liquid nitrogen freezing unit (Shenzhen De jie li Cryogenic Technology Co., Ltd.): feeding chain, freezing tunnel, PLC control unit, tunnel cover, distributing fans
Hollow-cone and Full-cone nitrogen spraying nozzles

requirements.rationale: The design uses tunnel temperatures from -70 °C (203.15 K) to -40 °C (233.15 K).
Cooling is by liquid nitrogen sprayed through nozzles in the tunnel; consumption is metered on the nitrogen pipe.
Whole fruits averaging 35.2 mm in diameter must pass through the freezing space.
Whole fruits averaging 36.09 mm in height must fit the clearance of the freezing space.
Freezing continues until the fruit core reaches -18 °C (255.15 K), so the space must be colder than that.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
